blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
승객: 기사님, 부산역으로 가 주세요.
기사: 부산역 몇 번 출구로 가실까요?
승객: 일단 부산역 주변으로 가 주세요.
기사: 알겠습니다.

…

승객: 여기서 내릴게요. 카드도 되나요?
기사: 네, 됩니다.
승객: 여기 있습니다.
기사: 감사합니다. 안녕히 가세요.
승객: 감사합니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Passenger: Please take me to Busan Station.
Driver: Which exit at Busan Station would you like to go to?
Passenger: Please take me near Busan Station for now.
Driver: All right.

…

Passenger: I’ll get out here. Can I pay by card?
Driver: Yes, you can.
Passenger: Here you are.
Driver: Thank you. Goodbye.
Passenger: Thank you.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text:
~로 가 주세요.
ro ga juseyo

여기
yeogi

~ 되나요?
~ doenayo

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: A passenger asks to go to Busan Station. The driver asks for a specific exit, but the passenger does not know the exact location and asks to go near the station first. At the end of the ride, the passenger asks to stop, checks whether card payment is available, pays, and exchanges polite goodbyes with the driver.

blocks.label: Dialogue · Korean
blocks.text:
직원: 몇 분이세요?
나: 두 명이요.
직원: 이쪽으로 앉으세요.
직원: 주문하시겠어요?
나: 좀 이따가 부를게요. 감사합니다.
직원: 네, 알겠습니다.

친구: 3인분 먹을까? 아니면 2인분?
나: 2인분만 하자.
친구: 그래.

나: 저기요, 주문할게요.
직원: 네, 말씀하세요.
나: 삼겹살 2인분하고 밥 두 공기 주세요.
직원: 음료는 뭐로 드릴까요?
나: 사이다 한 병 주세요.
직원: 네, 알겠습니다.

blocks.label: Dialogue · English
blocks.text:
Staff: How many people?
Me: Two.
Staff: Please have a seat over here.
Staff: Are you ready to order?
Me: We'll call you in a little while. Thank you.
Staff: Certainly.

Friend: Three servings? Or two?
Me: Let's just get two servings.
Friend: Okay.

Me: Excuse me, we'd like to order.
Staff: Certainly, go ahead.
Me: Two servings of pork belly and two bowls of rice, please.
Staff: What would you like to drink?
Me: One bottle of Sprite, please.
Staff: Certainly.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text:
몇 분이세요?
myeot bun-iseyo

좀 이따가 부를게요.
jom ittdaga bureulgeyo

주문할게요.
jumunhalgeyo

삼겹살 2인분, 밥 두 공기
samgyeopsal i-inbun, bap du gonggi

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: Two friends enter a restaurant and are shown to a table. They decide to choose their food before ordering, then call the staff when they are ready. They order two servings of pork belly, two bowls of rice, and a bottle of soda.

title: At work: asking someone to repeat
subtitle: Workplace · clarification · polite request

blocks.label: Dialogue
blocks.text:
A: 이건 오늘까지 끝내 주세요.
B: 죄송하지만, 다시 한번 말씀해 주세요.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: ‘다시 한번’ softens the request and frames it as one more attempt. ‘말씀’ raises the other person's speech politely.

blocks.label: Summary
blocks.text: Useful when instructions were unclear. You can reuse the same form in offices, hospitals, and public services.

title: At a restaurant: checking an order
subtitle: Restaurant · ordering · confirmation

blocks.label: Dialogue
blocks.text:
A: 이거 매운 거 맞아요?
B: 네, 조금 매워요.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: ‘맞아요?’ asks whether the listener confirms an assumption already in the speaker's mind.

blocks.label: Summary
blocks.text: Useful for confirming food, locations, names, schedules, and prices.

blocks.label: Notice
blocks.text: 덥네요.

blocks.label: Realize
blocks.text: 덥구나!

blocks.label: Insist
blocks.text: 덥다니까!

blocks.label: Hidden thought
blocks.text: The event is the same. What changes is the speaker's stance toward it.

blocks.label: Positive
blocks.text: 좋아요.

blocks.label: Negative
blocks.text: 나빠요.

blocks.label: Context
blocks.text: These words evaluate things, conditions, decisions, health, weather, and many other topics.

title: 예쁘다 / 아름답다
subtitle: Similar meaning, different scope and tone

blocks.label: 예쁘다
blocks.text: 예뻐요.

blocks.label: 아름답다
blocks.text: 아름다워요.

blocks.label: Difference
blocks.text: 예쁘다 is common and everyday. 아름답다 is broader and often more elevated or literary.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: 비가 와요.

blocks.label: Likely action
blocks.text: 우산을 가져가요.

blocks.label: Why it matters
blocks.text: This section connects words through ordinary expectations rather than dictionary definitions alone.

title: 손이 크다
subtitle: To prepare or give more than expected

blocks.label: Expression
blocks.text: 우리 어머니는 손이 커요.

blocks.label: Meaning
blocks.text: She tends to prepare a lot, especially food. It does not literally describe hand size.

blocks.label: Scene
blocks.text: A meal for three people becomes enough food for ten.

title: Notice
subtitle: The speaker notices or recognizes something in the moment.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “Oh, I notice that...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥네. → It's hot.
싫네. → I don't like it.
잘 아네. → So you konw it.
좋네. → It's good.
빠르네. → It's fast.

blocks.label: Naturalness
blocks.text: Some combinations are grammatically possible but uncommon without a suitable context. For example, '믿네' may sound marked or incomplete in ordinary conversation.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker encounters new information, notices a quality, or reacts to something happening in front of them.

title: Shared Knowledge
subtitle: The speaker treats the information as something both people know or can agree on.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “You know that too, right?”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥죠? → It's hot. right?
싫죠? → You don't like it. right?
믿죠? → You belive it right?
알죠? → You know it. Right?
맞죠. → It's correct. Right?

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker presents the statement as mutually accessible information and often expects agreement or confirmation from the listener.

title: Realization
subtitle: The speaker reaches a new understanding.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “Ah, now I understand...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥구나. → So it's truely hot.
그렇구나. → So that's it.
이 사람이 담당자군요. → So he is the person in the charge.
생각보다 멀군요. → So it is further than I thought.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker processes new information and expresses the moment of understanding or realization.

title: Guess
subtitle: The speaker infers something from available signs or circumstances.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I suppose...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥겠네요. → It looks hot.
힘들겠네요. → It looks hard.
많이 바쁜가 봐요*. → You look quite busy.
비가 오겠네요. → It seems it will rain.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker does not state the information as directly observed fact, but infers it from context, appearance, or prior information.

title: Insistence
subtitle: The speaker repeats or reinforces a claim.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I'm telling you...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
덥다니까. → I'm serious it's hot!
맞다니까. → I'm no lying!
괜찮다니까. → I'm surely fine!
진짜라니까. → It's really true!

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker strengthens a statement because the listener doubts it, disagrees, misunderstands, or has not responded appropriately.

title: Surprise
subtitle: The speaker reacts to something unexpected or more striking than anticipated.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “Oh, I didn't expect that...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
사람이 정말 많네요. → There are so many people.
생각보다 비싸군요. → It is more expensive than I expected.
벌써 다 끝났네요. → Oh, it is already finished.
한국어를 정말 잘하시네요. → You speak Korean very well.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker encounters something unexpected and immediately expresses surprise, admiration, or a mismatch with their previous expectation.

title: Confirmation
subtitle: The speaker checks whether their understanding or assumption is correct.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “My understanding is correct, right?”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
여기가 부산역 맞죠? → This is Busan Station, right?
내일까지 하면 되는 거죠? → I only need to finish it by tomorrow, right?
카드로 계산할 수 있나요? → Can I pay by card?
이 버스가 시청에 가는 거죠? → This bus goes to City Hall, right?

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker already has an assumption or partial understanding and asks the listener to confirm it before proceeding.

title: Reminder
subtitle: The speaker presents information as something the listener should already know or remember.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “You already know this...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
오늘 쉬는 날이잖아요. → You know today is a day off.
제가 아까 말씀드렸잖아요. → I told you earlier, remember?
여기는 주차하면 안 되잖아요. → You know we cannot park here.
그 사람 바쁜 거 알잖아요. → You know that person is busy.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker reminds the listener of information treated as already shared. Depending on tone, it may sound explanatory, persuasive, frustrated, or mildly reproachful.

title: Concession
subtitle: The speaker acknowledges one fact before introducing a limitation, contrast, or different conclusion.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “That is true, but...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
맛있기는 한데 너무 비싸요. → It is tasty, but it is too expensive.
좋기는 해요. 그런데 좀 멀어요. → It is good, but it is a little far away.
맞기는 한데 설명이 부족해요. → That is true, but the explanation is incomplete.
갈 수는 있는데 늦을 것 같아요. → I can go, but I think I will be late.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker accepts part of another person's statement or recognizes a positive point, while signaling that another concern changes the overall judgment.

title: Reluctance
subtitle: The speaker hesitates, avoids a direct refusal, or signals that something is difficult to accept.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I would rather not say no directly, but...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
오늘은 좀 어려울 것 같아요. → I do not think today will work.
그건 조금 곤란한데요. → That may be a little difficult.
지금 바로 결정하기는 좀 그래요<. → I am not comfortable deciding right now.
이번에는 참석하기 어려울 것 같습니다. → I do not think I can attend this time.

blocks.label: Pattern
blocks.text: Speaker is not confident it follows with certain signs ★'는'(but, though) '조금(좀)'(little) '약간'(few) '살짝'(a bit) '별로'(not) '그다지'(not so much) )

text.label: Situation
text.text: The speaker softens a refusal or negative judgment instead of stating it bluntly. Words such as 좀 and expressions such as 것 같아요 leave room for the listener to infer the refusal.

blocks.title: Concern
blocks.subtitle: The speaker notices a possible problem and expresses worry or consideration for another person.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I am worried about this...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
많이 힘드시겠어요. → That must be very difficult for you.
비가 많이 오는데 괜찮겠어요? → It is raining heavily. Will you be all right?
얼굴이 안 좋아 보여요. → You do not look well.
이렇게 늦어서 어떡해요? → What are we going to do now that it is so late?

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker infers that another person may be experiencing difficulty or that a situation may develop badly, and responds with sympathy, worry, or caution.

blocks.title: Intention
blocks.subtitle: The speaker presents a decision, plan, or immediate course of action.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “This is what I have decided to do...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
제가 다시 전화할게요. → I will call you again.
여기서 내릴게요. → I will get out here.
제가 확인해 보겠습니다. → I will check it.
이번 주말에는 집에서 쉬려고 해요. → I am planning to rest at home this weekend.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker communicates a decision or plan. 할게요 often responds to the immediate situation, while 하겠습니다 can sound more formal or deliberate.

blocks.title: Expectation
blocks.subtitle: The speaker anticipates a likely event or outcome based on current knowledge.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “This will probably happen...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
오늘은 늦게 끝날 것 같아요. → I think we will finish late today.
아마 주말에는 사람이 많겠어요. → There will probably be many people on the weekend.
이 길이 더 빠를 것 같아요. → I think this road will be faster.
아마 내일 도착할 거예요. → It will probably arrive tomorrow.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker predicts a future event or outcome. Unlike direct observation, the statement is presented as an expectation rather than a confirmed fact.

blocks.title: Regret
blocks.subtitle: The speaker looks back on an action or missed opportunity with dissatisfaction.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “I should have done something differently...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
택시를 탈 걸 그랬어요. → I should have taken a taxi.
미리 예약할 걸 그랬네요. → I should have made a reservation earlier.
그 말을 하지 말걸 그랬어요. → I wish I had not said that.
괜히 늦게 출발했어요. → I should not have left so late.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker evaluates a past choice negatively and imagines a better alternative that was not taken.

blocks.title: Reassurance
blocks.subtitle: The speaker tries to reduce another person's worry or resistance.

blocks.label: Hidden Thought
blocks.text: “You do not need to worry...”

blocks.label: Examples
blocks.text:
괜찮아요. 천천히 하세요. → It is all right. Take your time.
걱정하지 마세요. 제가 할게요. → Do not worry. I will do it.
시간 충분하다니까요. → I am telling you, we have enough time.
이 정도면 괜찮을 거예요. → This should be fine.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The speaker responds to another person's concern by presenting the situation as manageable, safe, or less serious than feared.
